segments.text: When a person is irradiated, the amount of radiation they have received is measured by the so-called dose.
segments.zh: 当一个人受到照射时，他所接受的辐射量是用所谓的剂量来衡量的。

segments.text: The dose is qualified usually by the words absorbed, equivalent or effective, to describe whether energy deposited or
segments.zh: 剂量通常会用“吸收”、“当量”或“有效”这些词来限定，以说明表达的是沉积的能量，还是

segments.text: associated local or whole-body biological damage is being conveyed.
segments.zh: 相关的局部或全身生物学损伤。

segments.text: The most basic dose is the absorbed dose.
segments.zh: 最基本的剂量是吸收剂量。

segments.text: This is the amount of energy that ionizing radiation deposits per unit mass on an irradiated material.
segments.zh: 它是电离辐射在受照物质上单位质量所沉积的能量。

segments.text: The units are the gray, and a dose of one gray
segments.zh: 单位是戈瑞，1 戈瑞的剂量

segments.text: represents the absorption of one joule of energy in the form of radiation by one kilogram of the material being irradiated.
segments.zh: 表示 1 千克受照物质吸收了 1 焦耳以辐射形式存在的能量。

segments.text: The definition of the gray in terms of mass means that the volume of the material
segments.zh: 戈瑞是以质量来定义的，这意味着

segments.text: irradiated to receive one unit dose depends on the density of that material. To illustrate this, consider three materials, air, water, and glass,
segments.zh: 要接受一个单位剂量的受照物质的体积取决于该物质的密度。为了说明这一点，我们来考虑三种物质：空气、水和玻璃，

segments.text: each receiving an energy of one joule over a material mass of one kilogram, i.e. a dose of one gray.
segments.zh: 每一种都是 1 千克的物质质量接受 1 焦耳的能量，也就是 1 戈瑞的剂量。

segments.text: Air is the least dense, so a cube of air 94 centimeters across the sides will be required.
segments.zh: 空气密度最小，所以需要一个边长 94 厘米的空气立方体。

segments.text: For water to receive the same dose, a cube 10 centimeter across will be required, while for glass,
segments.zh: 水要接受同样的剂量，需要一个边长 10 厘米的立方体，而玻璃

segments.text: which is dense than both air and water, a cube 7.4 centimeters across will be required.
segments.zh: 比空气和水密度都大，需要一个边长 7.4 厘米的立方体。

segments.text: Each of the cubes of material have the same mass, and each receive the same energy, so each would have the same absorbed dose.
segments.zh: 这几个立方体的质量相同，接受的能量也相同，所以它们的吸收剂量都相同。

segments.text: Looking at this from another viewpoint, consider a combined figure made of these three materials in equal volume, say a cube 10 centimeters on each side.
segments.zh: 换个角度来看，设想一个由这三种物质等体积组成的组合体，比如一个边长 10 厘米的立方体。

segments.text: Assume that this figure is irradiated, and that each region absorbs one joule of energy.
segments.zh: 假设这个组合体受到照射，每个区域都吸收了 1 焦耳的能量。

segments.text: Because each region has a different mass, each will have a different absorbed dose. The air region will have received
segments.zh: 由于每个区域的质量不同，每个区域的吸收剂量也就不同。空气区域接受的剂量是

segments.text: 833 gray, the water region 1 gray, and the glass 0.4 grays.
segments.zh: 833 戈瑞，水区域是 1 戈瑞，玻璃是 0.4 戈瑞。

segments.text: The effect of absorbing the energy is also different for the different materials.
segments.zh: 吸收能量所产生的效应对不同物质来说也是不同的。

segments.text: For example, consider the effect on the temperature of each of our one kilogram cubes of air, water, and glass
segments.zh: 例如，考虑一下对我们那三个 1 千克的空气、水和玻璃立方体的温度的影响，

segments.text: receiving an absorbed dose of, say, a thousand gray.
segments.zh: 假设它们接受的吸收剂量是 1000 戈瑞。

segments.text: This amount of energy is enough to raise the temperature of the cube of air by one degree Celsius.
segments.zh: 这么多的能量足以使空气立方体的温度升高 1 摄氏度。

segments.text: For water, the effect is much less, and a temperature rise of only one quarter of a degree Celsius will be seen, while for glass,
segments.zh: 对于水，影响就小得多，只会看到四分之一摄氏度的温升，而对于玻璃，

segments.text: the temperature rise would be larger than for both air and water at one and a quarter degree Celsius.
segments.zh: 温升会比空气和水都大，为 1.25 摄氏度。

segments.text: When the dose is typical of the limits applied to radiation workers in the public, and the material is biological in nature,
segments.zh: 当剂量处在适用于辐射工作人员和公众的限值的典型水平，而且物质是生物性的时，

segments.text: it is not the temperature rise that is of concern. Under these circumstances,
segments.zh: 令人担心的就不是温升了。在这种情况下，

segments.text: the concern is that cellular and genetic damage may lead to an increased risk of early death,
segments.zh: 令人担心的是细胞和遗传损伤可能导致过早死亡的风险增加，

segments.text: primarily through an increased likelihood of a future cancer development, or an increase in the likelihood of childbirth defects or inherited conditions.
segments.zh: 主要是通过增加未来发生癌症的可能性，或者增加出生缺陷或遗传性疾病的可能性。

segments.text: These effects are not only dependent upon the energy deposited by the radiation, but also by the type of radiation depositing the energy.
segments.zh: 这些效应不仅取决于辐射沉积的能量，还取决于沉积能量的辐射类型。

segments.text: For example, alpha radiation is highly ionizing due to its double charge, and because it is relatively easily slowed down,
segments.zh: 例如，α 辐射由于带两个电荷而具有很强的电离能力，而且由于它比较容易被减速，

segments.text: it deposits its energy over a short distance.
segments.zh: 它会在很短的距离内沉积能量。

segments.text: Because of this, it is 20 times more damaging per gray of absorbed dose than gamma radiation, as a gamma photon deposits far less energy per unit length of travel.
segments.zh: 正因为如此，每戈瑞吸收剂量下，它造成的损伤是 γ 辐射的 20 倍，因为 γ 光子在单位行程长度上沉积的能量要少得多。

segments.text: This leads to the concept of an equivalent dose, which is a measure of the biological damage and consequential risk of detrimental effects inflicted by ionizing radiation.
segments.zh: 这就引出了当量剂量的概念，它衡量的是电离辐射造成的生物学损伤以及由此产生的有害效应的风险。

segments.text: To obtain the equivalent dose, the absorbed dose is multiplied by a radiation weighting factor that accounts for its effect on biological tissues.
segments.zh: 要得到当量剂量，需要把吸收剂量乘以一个辐射权重因子，这个因子反映了辐射对生物组织的影响。

segments.text: The unit of equivalent dose is the C-vert. To obtain an equivalent dose of one C-vert requires an absorbed dose of one gray of gamma radiation,
segments.zh: 当量剂量的单位是希沃特。要得到 1 希沃特的当量剂量，需要 1 戈瑞的 γ 辐射吸收剂量、

segments.text: one gray of beta radiation, or one twentieth of a gray of alpha radiation, as alpha radiation is 20 times more damaging.
segments.zh: 1 戈瑞的 β 辐射，或者 1/20 戈瑞的 α 辐射，因为 α 辐射的损伤是 20 倍。

segments.text: The equivalent dose relates to relatively low doses and characterizes the increase in risk of detrimental effects.
segments.zh: 当量剂量针对的是相对较低的剂量，表征的是有害效应风险的增加。

segments.text: These are so-called stochastic effects, as they occur at random, and with a slightly increased probability of those members of the population who have not been irradiated.
segments.zh: 这些就是所谓的随机性效应，因为它们是随机发生的，而且比起那些没有受过照射的人群成员，发生的概率略有增加。

segments.text: The equivalent dose cannot be applied to acute exposure, where deterministic effects are seen.
segments.zh: 当量剂量不能用于急性照射，因为急性照射会出现确定性效应。

segments.text: Deterministic effects are a direct result of cell damage and occur when a given threshold of radiation exposure has exceeded.
segments.zh: 确定性效应是细胞损伤的直接结果，在辐射照射超过某个给定阈值时发生。

segments.text: Examples are erythema of the skin, induced sterility, and the formation of cataracts.
segments.zh: 例子有皮肤红斑、诱发不育以及白内障的形成。

segments.text: The response to an acute dose typically follows a sigmoid type curve, where the chance of developing symptoms is a function of the dose.
segments.zh: 对急性剂量的反应通常遵循一条 S 形曲线，出现症状的可能性是剂量的函数。

segments.text: Below the threshold, no effects are seen, while at the upper threshold, every patient would develop symptoms.
segments.zh: 低于阈值时看不到任何效应，而在上阈值处，每个病人都会出现症状。
